11:1.sourceText: Ἔστιν δὲ πίστις ἐλπιζομένων ὑπόστασις, πραγμάτων ἔλεγχος οὐ βλεπομένων.
11:1.targetText: Now faith is [the] substance of things hoped for, [the] proof of matters not being seen,

groups.note: The actual genitive plural being-hoped-for participle is substantival; English of things hoped for supplies its real nominal content without a separately written things noun.
The actual ὑπόστασις can denote underlying reality, assurance or confidence; LSV renders it substance. The actual noun is retained.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an article with substance; the actual predicate noun is anarthrous.
English supplies an article with proof; no corresponding Greek article is printed.

11:2.sourceText: ἐν ταύτῃ γὰρ ἐμαρτυρήθησαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.
11:2.targetText: for by this, the elders were well-attested.

groups.note: The actual passive testimony verb ἐμαρτυρήθησαν means they were attested/commended; English well-attested expresses that favorable testimony in context without an independent Greek well adverb.

11:3.sourceText: Πίστει νοοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας ῥήματι Θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι.
11:3.targetText: By faith we understand the ages to have been prepared by a saying of God, in regard to the things seen having not come out of things appearing.

groups.note: The actual εἰς τὸ introduces the explanatory/result infinitival proposition; English in regard to expresses that clause-introducing relation as a whole construction.

The actual article and seeing participle are neuter singular, what is seen; English uses the collective plural the things seen. The same actual visible content is retained with number and substantival support explicit.
The actual perfect becoming infinitive γεγονέναι is rendered having come in the English regard-to clause, retaining its coming-into-being head rather than a spatial coming verb.

11:4.sourceText: Πίστει πλείονα θυσίαν Ἄβελ παρὰ Κάϊν προσήνεγκεν τῷ Θεῷ, δι’ ἧς ἐμαρτυρήθη εἶναι δίκαιος, μαρτυροῦντος ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ δι’ αὐτῆς ἀποθανὼν ἔτι λαλεῖ.
11:4.targetText: By faith Abel offered a better sacrifice to God than Cain, through which he was testified to be righteous, God testifying of his gifts, and through it, he being dead, yet speaks.

groups.note: The actual comparative πλείονα, greater/more, is rendered better of the sacrifice; it remains this real comparative head, not a substituted κρείσσων adjective.
Actual dative article and first God noun jointly supply to God as the sacrifice recipient. The later genitive God occurrence in the testifying clause retains its distinct actual identity.
The actual dying aorist participle names Abel after death; LSV expresses the completed dying circumstance as he being dead. The same person/event head remains, not a separate written Greek be verb.

11:5.sourceText: Πίστει Ἐνὼχ μετετέθη τοῦ μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον, καὶ οὐχ ηὑρίσκετο διότι μετέθηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ Θεός. πρὸ γὰρ τῆς μεταθέσεως μεμαρτύρηται εὐαρεστηκέναι τῷ Θεῷ·
11:5.targetText: By faith Enoch was translated—not to see death, and was not found, because God translated him; for before his translation he had been testified to—that he had pleased God well,

groups.note: The actual μετατίθημι transfer/removal verb is rendered translated in the relocation sense; it does not mean changing a text from one language into another.

The actual translated-him object is the same Enoch named as possessor in the immediately restated translation event. English resumes that same participant as his translation; both realizations preserve the real translated person, not an independently printed second genitive pronoun.
The actual perfect passive has-been-attested predicate is rendered past perfect he had been testified to in the narrative; its actual testimony head remains.

The actual perfect pleasing-well infinitive gives the content of the attestation, with Enoch as its controlled subject. English expands that same content as that he had pleased ... well; no independent Greek he/that pronouns or separate well adverb are printed.

11:6.targetText: and apart from faith it is impossible to please [Him], for it is required of him who is coming to God to believe that He exists and [that] He becomes a rewarder to those seeking Him.

groups.note: The actual impersonal necessity verb δεῖ is rendered it is required of with its infinitive subject/participant construction; this is not a separately printed Greek passive requiring verb or of preposition.

Actual dative article and God noun jointly supply to God as the coming complement. The separately explained pleasing-object gap remains supplied; this case-phrase join does not invent an additional object occurrence.

English explicitly supplies the pleasing object. Pinned Greek has the pleasing infinitive without a written object here; the separate coming-to-God participant is not reassigned as an otherwise unexpressed object.
English repeats that before the second coordinated believed proposition; pinned N1904 has one ὅτι before He exists and no second that connector.

11:7.sourceText: Πίστει χρηματισθεὶς Νῶε περὶ τῶν μηδέπω βλεπομένων, εὐλαβηθεὶς κατεσκεύασεν κιβωτὸν εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ, δι’ ἧς κατέκρινεν τὸν κόσμον, καὶ τῆς κατὰ πίστιν δικαιοσύνης ἐγένετο κληρονόμος.
11:7.targetText: By faith Noah, having been divinely warned concerning the things not yet seen, having feared, prepared an ark to the salvation of his house, through which he condemned the world, and he became heir of the righteousness according to faith.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and house noun jointly supply of ... house as the salvation qualifier. His retains its separate actual personal-pronoun anchor.

11:8.sourceText: Πίστει καλούμενος Ἀβραὰμ ὑπήκουσεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τόπον ὃν ἤμελλεν λαμβάνειν εἰς κληρονομίαν, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν μὴ ἐπιστάμενος ποῦ ἔρχεται.
11:8.targetText: By faith Abraham, being called, obeyed, to go forth into the place that he was about to receive for an inheritance, and he went forth, not knowing to where he goes.

11:9.sourceText: Πίστει παρῴκησεν εἰς γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ὡς ἀλλοτρίαν, ἐν σκηναῖς κατοικήσας, μετὰ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ τῶν συνκληρονόμων τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῆς αὐτῆς·

groups.note: The actual εἰς introduces the land entered/inhabited as a sojourner; English in the land states the resulting dwelling domain, without replacing the written source by a different ἐν.

The actual foreign/another’s adjective ἀλλοτρίαν qualifies or stands for the land just named; English a strange country makes that repeated land designation explicit without another Greek country noun.

11:11.sourceText: Πίστει καὶ αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ δύναμιν εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος ἔλαβεν καὶ παρὰ καιρὸν ἡλικίας, ἐπεὶ πιστὸν ἡγήσατο τὸν ἐπαγγειλάμενον.
11:11.targetText: And by faith Sarah, herself barren, received power to conceive seed even after the time of life, seeing she judged Him who promised faithful;

groups.note: Pinned αὐτῇ is explicitly dative feminine singular, associated with dative Sarah; LSV presents herself as part of a nominative Sarah subject. The same Sarah-person identity is retained, with changed case/subject interpretation explicit rather than a fabricated nominative source form.

Pinned Σάρρᾳ is dative, confirmed by the N1904 N-DSF tag; LSV reads Sarah as subject of receiving. Sarah/Abraham subject constructions have been debated in this verse. This correspondence preserves the actual Sarah name and source case without deciding the disputed subject solely from morphology or altering the printed source to fit English.

The actual εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος is for deposition/laying-down or founding of seed/offspring, with καταβολή a noun, not a conceive verb. LSV verbalizes that whole procreative constituent as to conceive seed. Thayer2602 discusses the deposition/offspring and Sarah/Abraham subject alternatives; this mapping does not decide the disputed subject or sex-role interpretation, and does not invent a συλλαμβάνω lemma.
The actual παρά with the age/time limit means beyond/past the proper time; English after expresses that same exceeded limit in this age context, not a general παρά=after rule.

The actual third-singular judgment predicate is rendered she judged under the LSV Sarah-subject interpretation. Greek third-singular agreement alone does not identify the subject’s sex; the printed dative Sarah and interpretive alternatives remain explicitly noted above.

unmappedTarget.reason: The LSV adjective barren is absent from the exact pinned N1904 text, which has no στεῖρα token here. Other editions may print the adjective; no such word is added to this source.

11:12.sourceText: διὸ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑνὸς ἐγεννήθησαν, καὶ ταῦτα νενεκρωμένου, καθὼς τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει καὶ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος ἡ παρὰ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ ἀναρίθμητος.
11:12.targetText: for this reason, also, from one—and that of one who had become dead—were begotten as the stars of the sky in multitude, and innumerable as the sand that [is] by the seashore.

groups.note: The actual καὶ ταῦτα, and that/and this, emphasizes the added circumstance; neuter plural ταῦτα here resumes the circumstance rather than multiple new people.

targetPhrases.text: of one who had become dead

groups.note: The actual genitive perfect passive deadened participle refers to the previously named one. English of one who had become dead supplies that real substantival person support and recasts the passive deadened state as become dead; it does not print a new γίνομαι verb or settle literal bodily death from the form alone.

Actual dative article and multitude noun jointly supply in multitude as the numerical-respect phrase. The earlier stars/sky and later sand/seashore constituents remain separately linked; no independent Greek in preposition is printed.
The actual lip/edge-of-the-sea phrase is rendered by the compound seashore. Both real shore/edge and sea identities remain in the same compacted constituent without inventing an unrelated location.

11:13.targetText: All these died in faith, having not received the promises, but having seen them from afar, and having been persuaded, and having greeted [them], and having confessed that they are strangers and sojourners on the earth,

groups.note: The actual promises pronoun is the object both of seeing and of the immediately coordinated greeting. English resumes those same seen-and-greeted promises as bracketed them; no second Greek object is printed.

11:17.sourceText: Πίστει προσενήνοχεν Ἀβραὰμ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ πειραζόμενος, καὶ τὸν μονογενῆ προσέφερεν ὁ τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἀναδεξάμενος,

groups.note: The actual article plus μονογενής substantive identifies Abraham’s unique/only child in this offering event. English his states that same already specified Abraham-child relationship without a separate Greek possessive. 11:18.sourceText: πρὸς ὃν ἐλαλήθη ὅτι Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα,
11:18.targetText: of whom it was said, “In Isaac will your Seed be called,”

groups.note: The actual πρὸς ὃν with a saying predicate can be understood as addressed to whom or with reference to whom: Thayer4314 documents both directed-speech usage (including this verse) and the with-regard-to use after saying (including Hebrews1:7). LSV of whom is retained as that referential rendering. The father/son promise context and antecedent are not settled merely by English word order; this is not a source-witness phrase difference, and no different relative or preposition is invented.

The actual dative σοι is the promise recipient, for/to you seed will be named. English your Seed turns that same Abraham/offspring relation into a possessive; no written Greek genitive possessive is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual reporting ὅτι introduces the quotation; English directly quotes it without a separate that.

11:25.sourceText: μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος συνκακουχεῖσθαι τῷ λαῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἢ πρόσκαιρον ἔχειν ἁμαρτίας ἀπόλαυσιν,

groups.note: The actual συνκακουχέομαι compound states being mistreated together with; its with force belongs to that joint-suffering predicate, whose people complement is separately printed in the dative.

11:27.targetText: By faith he left Egypt behind, having not been afraid of the wrath of the king, for as seeing the Invisible One—he endured.

11:28.sourceText: Πίστει πεποίηκεν τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ αἵματος, ἵνα μὴ ὁ ὀλοθρεύων τὰ πρωτότοκα θίγῃ αὐτῶν.

groups.note: The actual perfect ποιέω, has done/observed, refers to keeping the Passover; English he kept retains that observing head, not the different Greek keeping verb τηρέω.

11:29.sourceText: Πίστει διέβησαν τὴν Ἐρυθρὰν Θάλασσαν ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς γῆς, ἧς πεῖραν λαβόντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι κατεπόθησαν.

11:37.targetText: they were stoned, they were sawn apart, they were tried; they died in the killing of the sword; they went around in sheepskins, in goatskins—being destitute, afflicted, injuriously treated,

groups.note: The actual goat adjective plus skins noun is rendered by the compound goatskins; both real source constituents remain retained in the one English word.

11:38.sourceText: ὧν οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος ὁ κόσμος, ἐπὶ ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι καὶ ὄρεσιν καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς.
11:38.targetText: of whom the world was not worthy; wandering in deserts, and mountains, and caves, and the holes of the earth;

11:39.sourceText: Καὶ οὗτοι πάντες μαρτυρηθέντες διὰ τῆς πίστεως οὐκ ἐκομίσαντο τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν,
11:39.targetText: and all these, having been testified to through faith, did not receive the promise,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

11:40.sourceText: τοῦ Θεοῦ περὶ ἡμῶν κρεῖττόν τι προβλεψαμένου, ἵνα μὴ χωρὶς ἡμῶν τελειωθῶσιν.
11:40.targetText: God, having provided something better for us, that apart from us they might not be made perfect.

groups.note: The actual προβλέπω foreseeing/providing-ahead verb is used for provision here (Thayer4265 explicitly cites this verse). English having provided retains that head, not a substituted ordinary giving verb.
